papers.title: Certified folding-free deformable image registration: A whole-cell Jacobian certificate and a sequential variational solver
papers.abstract: Registration maps propagate labels, measure local volume change, and map results back through their inverses; requiring invertibility. Voxelwise checks can miss folds between grid points. We study the canonical continuous extension of a nodal displacement field by trilinear interpolation and give a test that proves its Jacobian determinant positive in every grid cell or rejects the map. The test is rigorous under IEEE 754 binary64 arithmetic (correct rounding, no contraction). With a fixed boundary, certification implies a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism of the image domain. We introduce SeqVP, built around this certificate. A proximal Jacobian-determinant-curl formulation yields inner problems whose penalties on changes in the map, Jacobian determinant, and curl vanish to first order at the current iterate. The method decreases a fixed outer energy up to a floating-point resolution guard and certifies every committed iterate. After certified initialization, stopping at any time returns a folding-free map. A Poisson-preconditioned gradient method with Jacobian-aware step prediction and affine-scaling damping, initialized by certified handoff from an uncertified binary32 pre-optimizer, handles a 1 mm brain MRI with about 2e7 unknowns in 90 s on one GPU. On 49 held-out OASIS pairs, SeqVP achieves mean Dice 0.821 over 35 structures and 0.889 over 4 tissue classes, with certified zero folding. Gains are 0.022 and 0.025 over ANTs SyN, and 0.022 and 0.023 over uniGradICON with instance optimization at equal time (paired, Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), but maps are rougher. SeqVP is level with ANTs on LPBA40, behind it on IBSR18, and ahead of all label-free baselines on 20 large-deformation pairs. On fields from nine methods, the certificate finds non-positive-Jacobian cells in every ANTs SyN map (median 10, missed by voxelwise checks) and in maps from NiftyReg, ConvexAdam, uniGradICON, and TransMorph.

papers.title: Eddies that ride the flow: a model of turbulence with Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation
papers.abstract: We construct a divergence-free velocity field $\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x},t)$ on $\mathbb{T}^{n}$ that is a genuine function of position and carries both defining properties of turbulent transport: Richardson pair dispersion and a dissipative anomaly. No synthetic field has carried both, because the frame that gives the first destroys the field the second requires. The key is a dichotomy: deforming a spectrally localised pattern smears it across scales, whereas pushing its generating centres forward and re-convolving leaves the spectral envelope exactly invariant --- so transporting the eddy centres preserves both cascade and frame. In the field the finite-size Lyapunov exponent obeys $\zeta(R)=h(R)-1$ threshold by threshold within the scaling range, with a sweeping deficit $\Delta_{\rm sw}=+0.038\pm0.019$, consistent with zero, against $+0.091\pm0.019$ for the frozen field on the same data, a gap that doubles at Navier--Stokes intermittency. Companion papers prove that this family shows Richardson dispersion and a dissipative anomaly (Fefferman and Mayboroda 2026), and that a scalar advected by this flow obeys Yaglom's relation (De Lellis 2026), at small Kubo number. Trajectories forget their starting point as the smallest eddy is removed: the median separation of pairs released from one point with independent Brownian kicks varies as $\kappa_{p}^{0.0333\pm0.0038}$ over 22 decades of particle diffusivity, against $\kappa_{p}^{1/2}$ for a smooth control. A scalar in the same field closes the exact scale-by-scale variance budget, four independently measured terms balancing the dissipation to 15\% over 1.2 decades with no adjustable constant, and reaches its inertial--convective asymptote $S_{L}=-\chi r$ to $0.9995\pm0.0018$ once the measured diffusive transfer is restored, while under an imposed mean gradient $\chi$ changes by 14\% over a factor 5.8 in $\kappa$.

papers.title: Rigorously Certified Neural-Network Computation of Nonlinear Water Waves at Near-Machine Precision
papers.abstract: We present a computational framework that combines machine-learning-based discovery with rigorous computer-assisted numerical certification and formal verification for strongly nonlinear partial differential equations. We demonstrate the approach for periodic gravity-capillary traveling water waves. Physics-informed neural networks are used as a search mechanism, with the wave profile, wave speed and, in continuation experiments, surface tension learned directly from the governing equations without training data. Through a staged training and refinement procedure, the neural networks achieve near-machine-precision residuals of the governing equations, even in strongly nonlinear regimes. A single formulation recovers high-amplitude Stokes waves, Crapper waves and Wilton ripples. Continuation from a high-amplitude Wilton ripple in surface tension reveals new high-amplitude candidate solutions. We freeze one candidate as an explicit finite representation and rigorously certify a uniform bound on its governing-equation residual using interval arithmetic, accounting for floating-point roundoff, Fourier truncation, aliasing and grid-to-continuum errors. This independently validates the neural-network accuracy. We formalize the certification argument in Lean, which machine-checks the deductions from certified numerical bounds to the residual theorem. Both the interval certification and formalization were developed with substantial assistance from a large language model, while the validity of the result remains independent of the language model: the numerical bounds are rigorously enclosed by interval arithmetic and the subsequent mathematical deductions are checked by the Lean kernel. Together, these steps provide a pipeline from neural discovery to rigorous numerical certification and machine-checked verification with auditable mathematical guarantees.

papers.title: On blow-up dynamics for the nonlinear wave equation and the harmonic map heat flow
papers.abstract:
This Ph.D. thesis concerns the blow-up analysis, and more precisely, the asymptotic decomposition into profiles of solutions to nonlinear partial differential equations. In Chapter 1, we present a unifying framework for finding profile decompositions in Hilbert spaces using the notion of dislocation spaces. The next chapters are then devoted to my publications. In the second chapter, we construct solutions to the focusing, energy-critical, nonlinear wave equation in dimension 4 and 5, exhibiting finite-time Type II blow-up precisely at the origin with a single profile and a prescribed polynomial blow-up rate of order $-1-
u$, where $
u > 1$ in 4D and $
u > 3$ in 5D. The major difference between dimension 4 and 5 consists in the renormalization procedure. In 4D, we essentially follow the Krieger-Schlag-Tataru scheme developed for the 3-dimensional equation, where the polynomial structure of the nonlinearity permits the use of simple algebraic manipulations to control error terms. By contrast, the 5D case requires a modified setup due to the lower regularity of the nonlinearity, which complicates the treatment of nonlinear error terms. In Chapter 3, we provide a modern presentation of classical Lp and Schauder estimates for parabolic equations. Then, in Chapter 4, we consider finite-time and $k$-equivariant solutions to the harmonic map heat flow from a disk to a sphere. Under general time-dependent, $k$-equivariant and smooth boundary data, we prove that the profile decomposition at the singular time contains only one bubble. The method relies on the maximum and comparison principle. We also prove a global existence criterion and exhibit solutions blowing up in infinite time for any degree of equivariance. Finally, the appendix presents the profile decomposition for the harmonic map heat flow proved by Struwe and Qing using energy arguments and the Palais-Smale condition.

papers.title: Regularity Theory for the Equation $\det(D^2u) = f(u)$ in Two Dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the interior regularity of convex solutions to $$\det D^2u = f(u)$$ in planar domains, with no regularity or monotonicity assumptions on $f$. In particular, when $f$ is bounded between positive constants, we show that $u$ is locally $C^{1,\,1}$, and that its level sets near a critical point are asymptotically ellipses. Our analysis relies on a new monotone quantity for a second-order flow satisfied by the support functions of the level sets of $u$. As a byproduct of our methods, we obtain Liouville theorems that generalize a classical result of J\"{o}rgens, and include a complete classification of global solutions in 2D to an obstacle problem studied by Jin-Tu-Xiong. As another application, we obtain regularity and rigidity results for rotating-wave solutions of the semigeostrophic equations from meteorology.

papers.title: An Obukhov-Corrsin-Yaglom law for a kinematic model of turbulence
papers.abstract: We prove an Obukhov-Corrsin-Yaglom-type law for passive scalars advected by a family of random $C^\alpha$ velocity field proposed in \cite{JDEMS} as a kinematic model of turbulent fluids. Up to a technical assumption on one parameter, the expectation of the squared $L^2_t H^\gamma_x$ norm of solutions to the passive scalar equation is bounded by the squared $L^2$ norm of the deterministic initial datum, uniformly in the viscosity, whenever $\alpha + 2\gamma < 1$. The proof is based on a new insight in the theory developed by \cite{FM} to prove Richardson's dispersion and anomalous dissipation for the same model.

papers.title: Fundamental solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplacian in cone-like domains, with applications to Liouville-type theorems and global H\"older regularity
papers.abstract: Let $ C_\omega$ be the cone generated by a proper $C^2$ domain $\omega\subset\mathbb S^{N-1}$. We study positive homogeneous solutions of the fractional $p$-Laplace equation in $C_\omega$ with zero exterior values. For $p\ne2$, the operator is nonlinear and not uniformly elliptic. For every $p>1$, we identify two extremal homogeneities $\beta^+>0>\beta^-$, prove that every fundamental solution, if one exists, has one of these exponents, and construct homogeneous eigenfunctions whose eigenvalues have signs determined by the position of the homogeneity relative to $\beta^\pm$. As an application, we obtain the Lane-Emden threshold $q^*=p-1+sp/\beta^+$ for every $p>1$: nontrivial nonnegative supersolutions of $(-\Delta_p)^s u\ge u^q$ in $C_\omega$ do not exist for $0<q<q^*$, whereas homogeneous supersolutions exist for $q>q^*$. We also establish Hopf-type lower bounds at conical boundary points with the optimal exponent. When $p-1>sp$ , we construct both fundamental solutions, one singular at the vertex and the other vanishing there. For $p=2$, these solutions are known; our method recovers them for every $s\in(0,1)$. The homogeneous eigenfunctions also serve as barriers, yielding boundary decay and global H\"older regularity for $(-\Delta_p)^s u=f$ in bounded Lipschitz domains, with zero exterior values and $f$ continuous up to the boundary. The admissible H\"older exponents are determined by the exterior cones. All results hold for every $N\ge2$; in particular, $N>sp$ is not needed.

papers.title: Orbital stability and instability of standing waves for an inhomogeneous logarithmic Schr\"odinger equation
papers.abstract: We study the inhomogeneous logarithmic Schr\"odinger equation \[ i\partial_tu+\Delta u+|x|^{-1}u\log|u|^2=0, \qquad (t,x)\in\R\times\R^N,\quad N\ge2. \] For every initial datum in $H^1(\R^N)$, we establish global existence of weak solutions. We also construct explicit positive stationary solutions and solve the associated Nehari minimization problem. For $\omega\ge0$, the minimizer is unique up to {a constant} phase and is given by \[ e^{\frac{N-1}{2}(1+\sqrt{1+\omega})} e^{-(1+\sqrt{1+\omega})|x|}, \] whereas for $\omega<0$ the infimum is zero and is not attained. Finally, we prove that the standing waves associated with these profiles are orbitally stable for $\omega>0$ by a variational argument, and orbitally unstable for $-1<\omega<-1+(N-1)^{-2}$ by combining spectral analysis, localized energy and mass estimates, and phase modulation.

papers.title: Energy methods and optimal decay for time-fractional equations
papers.abstract: We study energy methods for the time-fractional equation $\partial_t^\alpha(u-u_0)-(a(t,x)u_x)_x+(F(t,x,u))_x=Q(t,x,u)$ on the real line, where $0<\alpha<1$, the coefficient $a$ is measurable and bounded from above and from below by positive constants, $\sigma\partial_xF\ge0$, $\sigma Q\le0$, and the data are in $L^1\cap L^\infty$. Using Yosida approximations of the kernel, an iteration on the $L^{2^m}$ norms gives the parabolic decay $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\le C\|u_0\|_{L^1}t^{-\alpha/2}$. In $L^2$ it gives the rate $t^{-\alpha/4}$, which, already for the linear equation, improves the rate $t^{-\alpha/5}$ obtained before by the classical energy method. For the convection--diffusion equation $\partial_t^\alpha(u-u_0)-u_{xx}+(|u|^{q-1}u)_x=0$, $q>1$, the parabolic rate is optimal for $q\ge2$, and for $1<q<2$ the convection improves it. An $L^1$ time-regularity estimate of B\'enilan--Crandall type gives the pointwise flux bound $|u|^{q-1}u-u_x=O(\|u_0\|_{L^1}t^{-\alpha})$. This bound takes the place of the Ole\u{\i}nik estimate and yields the optimal rate $\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim t^{-\alpha/q}$ for $1<q<2$. For nonnegative data, matching lower bounds hold for the $L^p$ norms.

papers.title: Multiplicity and least energy sign-changing normalized solutions for a Kirchhoff equation on bounded domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study sign-changing normalized solutions of the Kirchhoff problem \[ \begin{cases} -\left(a+b\displaystyle\int_\Omega|\nabla u|^2\,dx\right)\Delta u =|u|^{p-2}u+\mu u &\text{in }\Omega,\\ u=0 &\text{on }\partial\Omega, \end{cases} \] subject to the constraint \[ \int_\Omega |u|^2\,dx=c, \] where $a,b>0$, $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^N$ is a smooth bounded connected domain, $1\le N\le3$, $c>0$ is prescribed, and $\mu\in\mathbb R$ is a Lagrange multiplier. We assume $2<p<\infty$ for $N=1,2$ and $2<p\le6$ for $N=3$. For every integer $k\ge1$, we obtain at least $k$ distinct pairs of sign-changing normalized solutions for sufficiently small $c>0$. We determine the small mass asymptotics of their energies, Lagrange multipliers, and rescaled profiles in terms of the distinct Dirichlet eigenvalues and their eigenspaces. When $2<p<2+\frac{8}{N}$, we obtain infinitely many such pairs for every prescribed mass $c>0$, with energies tending to $+\infty$. At $p=2+\frac{8}{N}$, this conclusion holds for every sufficiently small fixed mass. We also establish the existence of a least energy sign-changing normalized solution on general bounded domains for every prescribed mass when $2<p<2+\frac{8}{N}$. For sufficiently small mass, such a solution exists on general bounded domains when $p=2+\frac{8}{N}$ and on star-shaped domains when $p>2+\frac{8}{N}$. For any family of such least energy solutions, the rescaled profiles approach the $L^2$-unit sphere of the second Dirichlet eigenspace in $H_0^1(\Omega)$ as $c\to0^+$. The finite multiplicity and least energy results include the Sobolev critical case $N=3$, $p=6$. The proofs combine a localized symmetric minimax construction, energy comparisons with one-signed critical points, and compactness arguments that preserve the sign-changing property.

papers.title: Non-migration for planar elastic flows
papers.abstract: We consider a closed planar curve evolving by the free or the length-preserving elastic flow. We prove that the scale-invariant bound $L\int k^2\,ds\le 4\pi^2+8/3$ at the initial time prevents the entire curve from crossing any line between two times. For the free flow, the proof combines a monotonicity estimate for the normalized bending energy with a barrier that compares centroid motion to an expanding energy radius. For the length-preserving flow, a quantitative gradient estimate controls the total centroid displacement.

papers.title: Well-posedness and large deviations for 3D primitive equations with jumps
papers.abstract: We establish the global pathwise well-posedness and a Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle for the three-dimensional viscous primitive equations driven by multiplicative L\'evy noise represented by a compensated Poisson random measure. Under local Lipschitz and moment growth assumptions on the noise coefficient, we construct local martingale solutions and obtain a unique maximal pathwise solution with c\`adl\`ag trajectories in the $H^1$ energy space. Additional sixth-moment growth in $H^1$ and $L^6$ growth bounds on the baroclinic component of the noise yield global pathwise well-posedness. The proof combines the jump It\^o formula with baroclinic and anisotropic energy estimates to rule out finite-time blow-up. Under further exponential integrability and structural assumptions on the noise coefficient, we establish a Freidlin--Wentzell large deviation principle in a strong path topology by the weak convergence approach.

papers.title: Boltzmann equations with dilatation and shear: global well-posedness and stability
papers.abstract: We study global well-posedness and stability for Boltzmann equations with linear velocity deformation, allowing for arbitrarily large deformation strength. For diagonal dilatation with $-2<\gamma\leq0$ and cylindrical dilatation with $-3/2<\gamma\leq0$, with or without shear, we construct global homogeneous solutions for small data and prove their stability under small spatially inhomogeneous perturbations. In scaled variables, the perturbations remain uniformly controlled in deformation-adapted spaces and decay in mixed spatial--velocity norms, algebraically in the diagonal regime and exponentially in the cylindrical regime. For homogeneous simple shear with $-2\leq\gamma\leq0$, we prove global existence and uniqueness for nonnegative data with finite mass and Fisher information, without smallness or a finite-energy assumption. These solutions conserve mass and propagate additional Sobolev regularity. For spatially inhomogeneous simple shear with $-2<\gamma\leq0$, we establish global well-posedness for small data. The analysis combines commuting vector fields, dispersive and bilinear collision estimates, and integrability of the rescaled collision coefficients. For homogeneous shear, a positivity-preserving splitting transfers Fisher-information control to rough data, while a Lorentz-space estimate includes the endpoint $\gamma=-2$ in the global continuation argument.

papers.title: Finite-Support Approximation in Variable-Coefficient Sobolev Spaces on Nonhomogeneous Flow-Measure Trees
papers.abstract: Let $T$ be a nonhomogeneous rooted tree equipped with a positive flow measure $m$. For $1<p<\infty$, consider the variable-coefficient Sobolev space on the nonhomogeneous flow-measure tree~$T$ \[ W_a^{1,p}(T,m) = \left\{ f\in L^p(T,m): \sum_{x\ne \rho}a(x)m(x)\lvert f(x)-f(\pi(x))\rvert^p<\infty \right\}, \] where $a$ is a positive variable coefficient, $\rho$ denotes the root and $\pi(x)$ denotes the parent of $x$. Using an averaging method over descendant levels, we prove the density of finitely supported functions in $W_a^{1,p}(T,m)$ for coefficients satisfying a weighted moment condition. As an application, the relationship between solutions on finite domains and global solutions is clarified for $p=2$.

papers.title: Infinitely many nonradial positive solutions for two-coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations in $\bbr^N$ without symmetry
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the following two-coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations: \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} &-\Delta u+P(x)u=\mu u^3+\beta uv^2,\quad\text{in }\R^N,\\ &-\Delta v+Q(x)v=\nu v^3+\beta u^2v,\quad\text{in }\R^N,\\ &u,\,v\in H^1(\R^N) \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $N=2,3$, $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ are potentials, $\mu$ and $\nu$ are positive coefficients and $\beta\in\R\setminus\{0\}$ is the coupling parameter. By developing the intermediate reduction arguments in [del Pino-Wei-Yao, Calc. Var., 2015], we prove the existence of infinitely many nonradial positive solutions to the above system under suitable regularity and decay conditions on $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$, {\bf but without any symmetry assumptions on them}. The scalar version of our result also gives {\bf a positive answer} to the first part of [Question~3, del Pino-Wei-Yao, Calc. Var., 2015] and our method might be helpful in studying other problems.

papers.title: Preservation and Loss of Log-Concavity in the Repulsive Vlasov--Poisson System
papers.abstract: Pr\'ekopa's theorem shows that, for jointly log-concave initial data, free transport preserves the log-concavity of spatial densities. This paper asks whether this property persists in the repulsive Vlasov--Poisson system. In dimensions two and higher, we construct smooth, strongly log-concave initial distributions whose spatial densities lose log-concavity at arbitrarily small positive times. For one-dimensional cold-ion data, we prove that the spatial density remains log-concave for all time.

papers.title: Asymptotic behavior of an integral equation of Landau-Lifschitz type
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study an integral equation of Landau-Lifschitz-type involving the Riesz potential $$ u(x)=\ell+C_*\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\frac{u(y)(|\nabla u(y)|^{2}+|u_k(y)|^2)-u_k(y)e_k}{|x-y|^{n-\alpha}}dy, $$ where $\ell \in \mathbb{R}^k$ is a constant vector, $C_* \neq 0$ is a constant, $u\colon\mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{S}^{k-1}:=\{u=(u_1,u_2,\cdots,u_k) \in {{\mathbb{R}}^{k}};|u|=1\}$, $k \geq 1$, $n \geq 2$, and $0<\alpha<n$. We provide a decay rate at which $|u_k|$ converges to zero under some mild conditions. This argument still works for the Ginzburg-Landau-type integral equation.

papers.title: The interface scattering law for run-and-tumble kinetic models
papers.abstract: For microorganisms with run-and-tumble motility, kinetic models provide a well-established description of transport in smoothly varying environments. Sharp signal changes, however, can induce asymmetric interface responses. A motivating example is the response to dark-light boundaries: cells moving into the light largely maintain their direction, whereas those entering the dark are effectively scattered back. Through an interface-layer analysis of pathway-based kinetic equations, we formally derive effective interface conditions for the limiting run-and-tumble model. These velocity-nonlocal conditions capture non-adiabatic scattering near signal discontinuities, linking intracellular sensory dynamics to transport across sharp environmental boundaries. For a two-velocity model, they reduce to an explicit transmission matrix. We assess the interface law numerically using biologically motivated parameters for E. coli chemotaxis.

papers.title: Finiteness of singularities for higher-weight axially symmetric minimizers of the relaxed Dirichlet energy
papers.abstract: Let $k\ge2$ be an integer. We prove that every minimizer of the Bethuel--Brezis--Coron relaxed Dirichlet energy in the signed meridional $k$-axial class, with continuous $H^1$ degree-zero data on the boundary of a ball, is smooth outside a finite subset of the symmetry axis. This extends the weight-one finiteness theorem of Hardt--Lin--Poon and resolves the finite-singularity question posed by Martinazzi--Rivi\`ere as Open Problem~A, in the fixed-boundary Bethuel--Brezis--Coron setting with continuous degree-zero data. The interior argument uses a distributional graph-boundary identity, height-preserving half-turn replacements, and exact square completions retaining the current cost. Cap-valued crosscuts and a finite incidence count exclude singular accumulation at the boundary poles.

papers.title: Dispersive estimates for Dirac equations in Aharonov-Bohm magnetic fields: massive case
papers.abstract: We study the dispersive properties of the massive Dirac equation perturbed by an Aharonov-Bohm magnetic field, proving in particular dispersive and Strichartz estimates for the associated flow. This paper is the natural continuation of our previous work in the massless case [3], and the overall structure of the analysis remains similar. The presence of a nonzero mass term, however, breaks the scaling invariance of the equation and introduces new difficulties at several stages of the argument. In particular, the appearance of the spectral thresholds +m and -m leads to a genuinely different low energy regime, which requires a separate analysis of the singular angular component.

papers.title: H^{s,p} estimates for weak solutions of fractional nonlocal equations in divergence form
papers.abstract: This paper establishes interior $H^{s,p}$ regularity for weak solutions to fractional nonlocal equations in divergence form with general kernels. Under the $(\delta, R)$-vanishing condition on the coefficients, we prove that for $p>2$, if the source term $f\in L^p_{loc}$, then the solution $u\in H^{s,p}_{loc}$. In contrast to Byun and Kim \cite{BK2025}, our result holds in the borderline case for $f$ without requiring differentiability assumptions. Our approach simplifies previous methods by using the stability properties of the fractional gradient to derive the good-inequality directly, thereby avoiding reliance on maximal functions. The proof integrates Vitali's covering lemma, Hardy-Littlewood maximal theory, self-improving estimates, and compactness arguments. This work extends classical $W^{1,p}$ regularity to fractional nonlocal settings under minimal kernel assumptions.

papers.title: Sharp singular Moser-Trudinger inequalities and n-Laplacian equations with degenerate potentials
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq2$, $0<\beta<n$, and let $V$ be a continuous nonnegative potential on $\R^n$ with a positive lower bound outside a ball. Under the constraint $\int_{\R^n}(|\nabla u|^n+V|u|^n)\dd\leq1$, we prove the singular Moser--Trudinger inequality with sharp coefficient $(1-\beta/n)\alpha_n$, where $\alpha_n=n|\mathbb S^{n-1}|^{1/(n-1)}$. The subcritical supremum is attained for every such potential. If $V$ is radial and $r^\beta V(r)$ is nondecreasing, the critical supremum is also attained. This includes potentials that vanish on a ball and decrease to a positive limit at infinity. Under the same radial hypothesis, a bound for the tangential gradient shows that every extremal is radial and that the tangential gradients of maximizing sequences converge to zero in $L^n$, including at the critical coefficient. For the singular $n$-Laplacian equation with critical exponential growth, we obtain an explicit sufficient level for Palais--Smale compactness. Under the Ambrosetti--Rabinowitz condition and a smallness assumption at zero, this gives a nonzero nonnegative mountain-pass solution for all sufficiently large coupling parameters.

papers.title: Classification and asymptotics for the boundary Yamabe equation with an isolated singularity
papers.abstract: We classify positive singular solutions of the boundary Yamabe equation on the punctured half-space in every dimension $n\ge3$. Previous symmetry results reduce this problem to a nonlinear PDE in two variables, for which classical phase-plane methods are unavailable. We develop a Hamiltonian method that combines local bifurcation with compactness to prove that every nonstationary cylindrical profile of a singular solution is periodic and uniquely determined, up to translation, by its Hamiltonian energy. At each stationary or periodic profile, the space of solutions of the linearized equation is two-dimensional. Finally, every positive solution in a half-ball with a nonremovable isolated boundary singularity is asymptotic to a unique global singular solution, with an algebraically decaying relative error.

papers.title: Determination of the Lam\'e parameters and density at a fixed frequency
papers.abstract: We establish global uniqueness for the inverse boundary value problem of three-dimensional time-harmonic isotropic elasticity with smooth real Lam\'e parameters satisfying strong convexity and a smooth positive mass density. At a fixed known nonzero frequency for which the corresponding Dirichlet problems are uniquely solvable, the full displacement-to-traction map uniquely determines all three coefficients. The proof first recovers the full boundary Taylor expansions of $\lambda$, $\mu$, and $\rho$, and derives an exact Green--Betti identity for a four-component reduction, with the terms involving $W=\omega^2\rho$ and $\nabla W$ retained. Three independent physical polarizations of the rank-three characteristic quotient yield a complete $3\times3$ matrix of polynomial moment identities. A Cauchy transform construction produces an exact relative transport matrix $H$, normalized to $I_3$ in a common exterior region. Its invertibility follows from the determinant identity $\det H=\sqrt{\mu_2/\mu_1}>0$. Holomorphic dependence on the projective null direction, established by differentiating the transport equation at a fixed physical point, leads to a finite-type rigidity system that determines the Lam\'e parameters. Finally, products of physical elastic solutions and Fourier uniqueness recover the mass density.

papers.title: Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation for the random velocity model with controlled sweeping
papers.abstract: The present paper establishes the Richardson dispersion law, predicting the particle separation with time according to $\E R_t^2 \sim t^3$, as well as anomalous dissipation for the associated tracer, for a random H\"older continuous velocity vectorfield with controlled sweeping.

papers.title: Critical Curve for Three-Dimensional Radial Wave Systems with Distinct Speeds
papers.abstract: We study radially symmetric solutions to the three-dimensional semilinear wave system with distinct propagation speeds \[ u_{tt}-c_1^2\Delta u=|v_t|^p\ , \ v_{tt}-c_2^2\Delta v=|u_t|^q\ , \ c_1, c_2>0\ , c_1\neq c_2\ . \] For \(1<p,q<2\), we prove that \[ \Gamma(p,q) = 2+\max\left\{\frac1p,\frac1q\right\}-pq=0 \] is the exact critical curve separating small-data global existence from finite-time blow-up. More precisely, sufficiently small, compactly supported radial initial data give rise to global solutions when $\Gamma(p,q)<0$. On the other hand, for a class of initial data, the corresponding solutions blow up in finite time, with an upper bound for the lifespan, when $\Gamma(p,q)\geq 0$.

papers.title: Global existence of solutions to the 2D compressible nematic liquid crystal flows with large initial data and vacuum
papers.abstract: For periodic initial data that allow vacuum, we establish the global-in-time existence of solutions to the 2D compressible nematic liquid crystal flows, under the condition that the bulk viscosity coefficient is sufficiently large and a geometric angular constraint is imposed on the initial direction field. Our results remain valid for arbitrarily large initial energy. Furthermore, under appropriate additional assumptions imposed on the pressure, we also establish the uniqueness of the constructed solutions.

papers.title: Global well-posedness for the energy-critical focusing NLS on $\mathbb T^3$
papers.abstract: We prove global well-posedness for the focusing quintic nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation on the standard three-dimensional torus for initial data below the mass-corrected energy and Sobolev-norm thresholds determined by the Euclidean ground state. This gives a subthreshold focusing counterpart to the defocusing theorem of Ionescu and Pausader. The proof combines the periodic profile analysis with the recent nonradial Euclidean scattering theorem of Su and Zhao. The mass correction yields an invariant region and a nonnegative energy decomposition, placing every Euclidean profile below both ground-state thresholds. Uniform bounds on finite intervals follow from a contradiction argument on shrinking time intervals.

papers.title: Second-order geometric consistency of nonlinear FE-HMM on surfaces via corrector non-degeneracy
papers.abstract: We analyze the geometric variational crime of nonlinear finite element heterogeneous multiscale methods (FE--HMM) for $p$-growth monotone laws on curved surfaces, $p\ge2$. The practical method projects discrete gradients onto the exact tangent planes; we compare it with the exactly lifted method on the same discrete space. Without further hypotheses, the difference is $O(h_g^{p/(p-1)})$ in the metric induced by the cell correctors. The optimal order $O(h_g^2)$ holds with a constant given by a weighted negative moment of the corrected gradients, evaluated along the practical solution only; no bounds on discrete gradients in $L^\infty$ are used. The negative moment is a sufficient condition for the lower shifted $p$-structure of the discrete homogenized flux, which for $p>2$ is not available in general. For the model law and a fixed cell mesh, its uniform boundedness is equivalent to a finite-dimensional directional criterion on degenerate correctors, and for laminates it holds with an explicit bound, uniform in the cell mesh. With macro--micro quasi-optimality and an estimate for coefficient sampling, the reconstructed microscopic field converges as $O(h+H^{\min{s,1}}+h_g^2)$, where $H^s$ is the cell approximation rate. Experiments on a torus with an exact closest-point lift and a transported anisotropic $p=4$ material show second-order geometric convergence up to $98,304$ macroscopic quadrature points, each with a fully solved nonlinear cell problem, with bounded a posteriori constants for both load treatments.

papers.title: Instability of Self-Similar Implosions for the Compressible Euler Equations
papers.abstract: We prove that all known regular self-similar implosion solutions of the isentropic compressible Euler equations are unstable to shock formation. The perturbations can be chosen to be small in a class determined by the regularity threshold of the background. The proof relies on an amplification mechanism which occurs along the surface of the backward sonic cone from the implosion point. Motivated by our main results, we formulate an implosion censorship conjecture for the compressible Euler equations, stating that classical implosions are unstable to shock formation.
